DORMANT_POINTS contains only HookPoint.ARTIFACT_CREATED (artifact.created). It has no production emit site, so handlers registered on it are accepted but never fire. _BLOCKING_POINTS contains HookPoint.TOOL_PRE (tool.pre) and HookPoint.USER_PROMPT_SUBMIT (prompt.submit). These points propagate handler exceptions so a guard can veto the action. Source: lionagi/hooks/bus.py, DORMANT_POINTS at line 71 and _BLOCKING_POINTS at line 76.

Two calls in _make_api_agent_spec (lionagi/cli/agent.py:257-273). (1) It sets spec.coding_tools = _API_TOOL_SETS[tools] at agent.py:271. _API_TOOL_SETS is defined at agent.py:83 as {'read': ('reader', 'search', 'context')}, so for the read tool set spec.coding_tools becomes ('reader', 'search', 'context'). (2) It calls _wire_secure_guards(spec, cwd) at agent.py:272, imported from lionagi/agent/spec.py and defined at spec.py:44. That function registers guard_destructive on the security_pre:bash bucket, and guard_paths(allowed_paths=[cwd or Path.cwd()]) on the security_pre:reader and security_pre:editor buckets (spec.py:52-56). The test at tests/cli/test_agent_api_provider.py:478 asserts the same tuple.

The guards are wired by `_wire_secure_guards(spec, cwd)` (lionagi/cli/agent.py:272). It is imported from `lionagi.agent.spec` at line 266. Its body has not been read, so I cannot yet confirm how it installs the path guard scoped to `cwd`.

The two calls, in order: `AgentSpec.compose(role, ..., tools=["coding"], ...)` builds the base spec, then `spec.coding_tools` is overwritten with the API set, and finally `_wire_secure_guards` attaches the guards.

_wire_secure_guards (lionagi/agent/spec.py, lines 44-56) registers two handler functions. First, guard_destructive is registered via obj.security_pre("bash", guard_destructive). Second, guard_paths is called as guard_paths(allowed_paths=[workspace_root]), where workspace_root is cwd or Path.cwd(). The resulting path_guard is registered on two tools: obj.security_pre("reader", path_guard) and obj.security_pre("editor", path_guard). So the path guard covers reader and editor, and the destructive-command guard covers bash. All registrations go to the security_pre bucket, not the user pre bucket, so they take part in the security -> user -> security recheck (ADR-0086 delta row 1). The function is called from AgentSpec.coding() when secure=True (line 154).

_wire_secure_guards (lionagi/agent/spec.py:44-56) registers two hook handlers, both in the security_pre bucket. First, guard_destructive is registered on the bash tool (line 52). Second, a single path guard is registered on the reader tool and on the editor tool (lines 55-56). Trace of the guard_paths registration: line 50 imports guard_destructive and guard_paths from lionagi.agent.hooks. Line 53 sets workspace_root to cwd, or Path.cwd() if cwd is None. Line 54 calls guard_paths(allowed_paths=[workspace_root]), which is the factory at lionagi/agent/hooks.py:87. It returns the async _guard closure, with no denied_paths. That same closure object is passed to security_pre for 'reader' and for 'editor'. Each call appends to hook_handlers under the key 'security_pre:<tool>' (spec.py:31-33). _wire_secure_guards is called from AgentSpec.coding when secure=True (spec.py:154), from lionagi/cli/agent.py:272, and from lionagi/engines/engine.py:523. When LIONAGI_HOME is unset, it defaults to ~/.lionagi, built as Path.home() / '.lionagi' and then expanded with expanduser() in lionagi/_paths.py line 20. lionagi/mcp/config.py imports LIONAGI_HOME and RUNS_ROOT from lionagi._paths at line 16. It derives two constants: RUNS_DIR = RUNS_ROOT (config.py line 19), where RUNS_ROOT is LIONAGI_HOME / 'runs' (_paths.py line 21), so RUNS_DIR is ~/.lionagi/runs; and JOBS_DIR = LIONAGI_HOME / 'mcp' / 'jobs' (config.py line 23), so JOBS_DIR is ~/.lionagi/mcp/jobs.
